newsitem.title: CHINA: Earthquakes rock northwest China - officials.
newsitem.headline: Earthquakes rock northwest China - officials.

text.p: A series of earthquakes jolted China's northwestern Xinjiang region early on Wednesday, with the strongest measured at 6.3 on the Richter scale, officials said.
Local officials said rescue teams were being sent to check for casualties from the latest earthquakes to rock Xinjiang's Jiashi county, where nine people were killed in a tremor last week.
"We don't expect deaths because everyone has been living in tents for fear of earthquakes since the beginning of the year," an official of the Jiashi seismological bureau said by telephone.

The larger earthquake, which registered 6.3 on the Richter scale, rocked Jiashi county at 2.19 a.m. (1819 GMT Tuesday) and was followed by at least two smaller tremors, an official of the seismological bureau in the nearby city of Kashgar said.

"One earthquake felt very strong and our tent fell down," said a local broadcast official in Jiashi. Nine people were killed and 60 injured in Jiashi last week after a powerful earthquake measuring 6.6 on the Richter scale.
Officials had forecast more earthquakes of more than six on the Richter scale.
"We think the earthquake last night was the one that had been forecast," the Jiashi seismological official said. "But there could still be more."
Most residents of Jiashi, an area of cotton farmers and sheep herders, have been living in tents since a major earthquake in January that has been followed by thousands of aftershocks and tremors.
Most of the older dwellings in the town of 270,000 residents had been flattened and the tremors had damaged many of the newer multi-story buildings.

Jiashi county lies at the meeting of the Pamir-Lake Baikal seismological belt and the seismological belt of the Himalayas, making it an area vulnerable to frequent tremors, seismological officials said.
In 1961, three earthquakes measuring more than six on the Richter scale jolted Jiashi, and aftershocks continued for 20 months, a seismological official said.
